cards.title: Introduction to Algorithms
cards.content:
An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem or completing a task. In Python, we use efficient algorithms to process data structures quickly.

# A simple algorithm to find the maximum number
def find_max(numbers):
    max_val = numbers[0]
    for num in numbers:
        if num > max_val:
            max_val = num
    return max_val

cards.title: Understanding Big O Notation
cards.content:
Big O notation describes the performance or complexity of an algorithm, specifically how scaling the input size affects execution time or memory usage.

  • O(1): Constant time
  • O(n): Linear time
  • O(n^2): Quadratic time

content.text: An algorithm whose execution time directly and linearly scales with the input size has a Big O complexity of O(__1__).

cards.title: Sorting Algorithms
cards.content:
Sorting arranges data in a particular order. Common algorithms include Bubble Sort, Merge Sort, and Quick Sort.

Python's built-in sorted() and list.sort() use Timsort, a hybrid sorting algorithm derived from merge sort and insertion sort.

cards.title: Searching Algorithms: Linear vs Binary
cards.content:
Searching is the process of finding a specific item in a collection.

Linear Search: Checks every element one by one. Works on unsorted data. O(n).

Binary Search: Repeatedly divides a sorted collection in half. Much faster with O(log n).

# Binary Search implementation in Python
def binary_search(arr, target):
    low, high = 0, len(arr) - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if arr[mid] == target:
            return mid
        elif arr[mid] < target:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid - 1
    return -1

items.text: Initialize low and high pointers at the start and end of the sorted array.
Compare the middle element with the target value.
Adjust pointers (low or high) based on the comparison to narrow the search range.

cards.title: Recursion and Memoization
cards.content:
Recursion occurs when a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem. Dynamic programming uses memoization to cache results of expensive function calls.

# Fibonacci with memoization using functools
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fibonacci(n):
    if n < 2:
        return n
    return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)

cards.title: Conclusion
cards.content: You have reviewed the core concepts of algorithms in Python, including Big O notation, searching, sorting, and recursion. Practice implementing these to write optimized code!
